source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #352 (branch fix/334-borrowed-drop at head 71b3bce86c8db4431cc55a36fa3e35fb1b2db662 — the #334 change (a borrow of an owned resource can no longer be dropped while the borrow is outstanding, and ownership transfer of a borrowed resource is rejected), as revised by the second Codex review round (transferred borrows are registered against the originating resource’s identity — a process-unique record id carried through the transfer — instead of being resolved by rep, which guest code can duplicate across distinct resources) merged with current main b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b (PR #353); the merge conflicted only in the size-baseline files, resolved by taking main’s versions; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45596144363, 45596163457 and 45596181128 against the branch and pull-request run 45595313921, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #352 (#334, a borrow of an owned resource can no longer be dropped while the borrow is outstanding, and ownership transfer of a borrowed resource is rejected), the branch’s second: the second Codex review round found that the round-1 registration of transferred borrows resolved the lent resource’s owned entry by rep, but reps are guest-chosen and two distinct resources can share one, so a transferred borrow could be registered against an unrelated owned entry; transferred borrows are now registered against the originating resource’s identity — a process-unique record id minted when the record is allocated and carried through the transfer alongside the handle. The branch merged current main (merge commit 71b3bce86c8db4431cc55a36fa3e35fb1b2db662, main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b — PR #353 (#318, split extern-name encodings decode and extern names are validated against the package-name grammar) on top of the main at d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3 the branch was based on); the merge conflicted only in tools/embedder-size-baseline.json and docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, resolved by taking main’s versions of both, and its CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate on the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45596195660, 45597833259 and 45597846454 on main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b; all three runs pass the gate against main’s checked-in baseline). Against the checked-in baseline, the main control is byte-identical on all 32 gated series. This PR’s own delta against the main control is confined to the same 12 series: in release, stripped file +9,416 B (component), +9,400 B (wasi) and +9,400 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +8,720 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +6,296 B / +6,296 B / +6,312 B and stripped .text +5,040 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. All twelve series exceed the checked-in baseline, so those twelve are re-baselined to the branch measurements. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release component stripped file series at +11.41% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,272 B), up from +11.02%; the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
